model_meta.description: Concept-level structural and behavioral model of a telescoping fluid cylinder using staged piston movement and poppet-controlled flow paths.

subsystems.description: Cylinder housing 22 encloses interior region 82. In the preferred embodiment, head cover 20 contains cavity 66 and port 64; distinct rod cover 18 has port 128. Claim 1 recites a cylinder cover cavity and generalized first/second pistons, not explicitly equated with preferred-embodiment inner/outer pistons.

parts.description: Head-cover flow-control valve 80 adjusts airflow received through port 64.

ports.name: Rod-cover air port 128 (exhaust destination during initial extension; pressure inlet during retraction)

subsystems.description: Preferred embodiment outer piston 84 travels in housing interior 82 and couples to outer rod 34; it carries poppet cavities and passages. This embodiment-specific mapping is not an assertion it is claim 1's first piston: claim 1 distinguishes a first piston too large for the cover cavity from a second piston fitted in that cavity.

interfaces.interface_type: pneumatic exhaust flow during initial extension

subsystems.description: Preferred embodiment inner piston 70 is in head-cover cavity 66 and couples to inner rod 46, which passes through outer piston 84 and outer-rod channel 48. These embodiment labels are not automatically equivalent to claim 1's first/second piston labels.

ports.name: Inner rod axial motion within outer rod

interfaces.interface_type: nested and coordinated axial rod motion

subsystems.description: Poppets, shafts, and seals selectively open or close air paths through the outer piston as the pistons move.

External operating context representing pneumatic pressure applied at head-cover port 64 for extension and rod-cover port 128 for retraction. Supply internals and switching equipment are not modeled; the patent separately describes a switch block in the operating context without establishing it as part of this pressure-source subsystem.
External tool/workpiece acted upon by the telescoping rods.

item_flows.name: Pneumatic pressure supply
item_flows.notes: Pressure is applied at head-cover port 64 during extension and at rod-cover port 128 during retraction; no internal supply or switching topology is asserted.

item_flows.name: Internal air flow
item_flows.notes: During initial extension, air ahead of inner piston 70 passes through outer-piston cavities 88/90 and chambers 98, then exits the cylinder at rod-cover exhaust port 128; after pistons contact, seals close this path.

item_flows.name: Telescoping axial motion
item_flows.notes: Relative and coordinated motion of inner and outer rods.

item_flows.name: Workpiece interaction
item_flows.notes: Rod/tool contact transfers force to workpiece.

requirements.statement: The cylinder shall permit inner-rod movement relative to the outer rod and coordinated movement of both rods during the stroke.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1 supports structural piston/rod arrangement only. Independent initial movement followed by contact and joint movement is described in the abstract and preferred-embodiment operation, not as claim 1 behavior.

requirements.statement: The poppet arrangement shall control air paths through the outer piston by opening and sealing the paths as piston positions change.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1 supports a poppet held in an aperture. Air-path opening/closing is described for preferred-embodiment cavities and seals, not as operating behavior recited in claim 1.

requirements.statement: The poppet length shall stop the claim-defined second piston from forward movement before the claim-defined first piston contacts the rod cover.
requirements.rationale: Claims 4–5 specify poppet contact with rod cover closing the first-piston aperture and poppet length stopping the second piston before the first piston contacts the rod cover. Preferred embodiment instead describes valves stopping inner piston 70 while outer piston 84 continues; labels are not asserted as claim-number equivalents.

steps.description: During preferred-embodiment extension, pressure is applied through head-cover port 64. Inner piston 70 moves forward independently; air ahead passes through poppet cavities 88/90 around shafts and exits rod-cover port 128.
When inner piston 70 contacts outer piston 84, poppet seals close cavities 88/90; pressure through port 64 then acts on both pistons, which move together.
At the forward end, poppets contact the rod-cover inner surface and prevent inner-piston forward movement while outer piston 84 continues forward.
During retraction, pressure is applied at rod-cover port 128; outer piston 84 and inner piston 70 move in unison while valves 92/94 remain seated.
The cited description does not specify the exhaust destination during this retract sequence; no exhaust route is asserted.
